    - Morwen. I teach magic at the Academy. Speak plainly, *Player*, I have a class in a quarter of an hour.

    - Young mages. The first thing I tell them is that magic is mostly patience. The second, usually within the hour, is to stop showing off.
    - The good ones are afraid of me for a year. After that they discover I am the best teacher in the Quarter. The rest discover I remember everything.
    - My family has gathered what survived of the Magicians' seal-craft since the Balrog War: notes, half a diagram, letters that mention a working and then break off. I am putting them back together.
    - I do not know how the seal was finished, or how it might be mended, and anyone who tells you they do is lying. I know more than most about how it was begun. That is all.
    - [Everard](../npcs/everard.md). A student of mine who sleeps through my lectures and passes every exam. He could be a great mage if he tried. He will not try.
    - And there is one piece in my family's chest I have never shown anyone. Do not ask me what it is. Not yet.
    - Go on, then. Patiently.
    - He came on the practical. He tried, for about a minute, when he thought I was not looking. I was looking. It was enough to begin with.
